newsitem.title: CHINA: China says illegal garbage imports stopped.
newsitem.headline: China says illegal garbage imports stopped.

text.p: Illegal imports of garbage, which helped push Sino-U.S. relations to a low in 1996, have been halted due to heavy penalties and more careful customs checks, the China Daily Business Weekly reported on Sunday.
U.S. businessman William Ping Chen was sentenced to 10 years in jail last month in Shanghai on charges of illegally importing restricted garbage and is awaiting a ruling on his appeal.

The newspaper said that since tough regulations were imposed in April last year, the only cases of illegal garbage imports reported were several batches of radioactive scrap metal stopped in the northern port of Tianjin.
A total of 49,000 tonnes of garbage was found amongst two million tonnes of reclaimable material inspected by customs officials last year, hidden amongst scrap paper or metal shipments, it said.
It quoted an official report as saying foreign scrap suppliers, including the United States, Russia and Japan, had become more cautious.

"Standard and sizable suppliers from the United States plan to take extra care with their deliveries to China, for fear that quality problems will affect their reputation and share of the massive market," the report said.

The jailed U.S. businessman, born in Shanghai and now a resident of Oakland, California, was sentenced to deportation and a 500,000 yuan ($60,000) fine as well as a jail term after confessing to smuggling 238 tonnes of garbage and medical waste.
He was arrested in June last year and sentenced following a hearing on December 2.

Chen's arrest was the climax of an emotional campaign launched by China in mid-1996 over illegal shipments of U.S. garbage listed as waste paper for recycling but found to contain old clothes, rubber gloves, and disposable syringes.

Chen had listed the imports as waste paper and mixed paper, and proceeded with the shipments despite warnings from Shanghai environmental officials and opposition from his Chinese joint venture partners, the official Xinhua news agency said.
